newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks seen in tight range, eyes on yen.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks seen in tight range, eyes on yen.

text.p: Tokyo stocks are expected to drift in a tight range on Tuesday with investors eyeing the yen, which has slipped past 116 to the dollar and may encourage purchases of blue-chip issues, brokers said. They said trade is likely to be slow on what is the last day for May delivery.
On Monday, the 225-share Nikkei average gained 34.50 points, or 0.17 percent, to finish at 20,043.50. Its June futures were up 120 points at 20,150.
"Trade should be even more subdued today than it was on Monday as dealers especially will hold off on taking up new positions," a broker at a second-tier brokerage said.
Turnover on Monday was light, with 269 million shares changing hands on the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange, down from 368 million on Friday.

Investors continued to flock to shares involved in the integrated circuit (IC) related business. Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp said it plans to begin converting its public phones into ones that use IC cards in the near future.
Mitsubishi Plastics Industries Ltd, one such share, was the second largest percentage gainer on the first section. It rose 41 yen or 9.76 percent to stand at 461.
Telecommunications equipment maker Tamura Electric Works added 41 yen to stand at 936. Shinko Electric Co, a electrical machinery maker, was bid-only at 502, after closing at 467 yen on Monday.
Shares of Oki Electric Industry Co Ltd slumped 23 yen to stand at 583 on grim group earnings announced on Monday.
On the other hand, electric wire and cable maker Fujikura Ltd surged to a high for calendar 1997 on a robust earnings announcement. It stood at 993 yen, up 15 yen.

"The market will be even more lost for direction once the earnings announcement peak is over," a broker at a second-tier brokerage said. "Hopefully, the industrial production data due out later this week will make investors confident over the health of the economy and encourage them to buy."
Preliminary industrial production figures for April and forecasts for May and June are due out on Thursday.
In sectors, transport equipment, non-ferrous metals, trading houses, insurance and iron/steel were at the top of the list of gaining sectors.
Ship building, real estate, sea transport, miscellaneous manufacturers and oil headed the list of retreating sectors.
In other indices, the TOPIX slipped 2.60 points or 0.17 percent to stand at 1,492.01. The Nikkei 300 shed 0.66 point or 0.23 percent to stand at 288.60.
